layers.cairn: Cairn Store (Rust, S3 API). Clusters with replicas, erasure coding and racks/zones; versioning and object lock; SSE, with customer-managed keys in Vault Transit; STS temporary credentials; lifecycle and tiering; backups, continuous backup and two-way sync; WebDAV, SFTP, FUSE, CSI and Hadoop S3A; node TLS

Cairn Catalog (Rust, Iceberg REST). Tables and views; Delta Lake tables through Trino, registered by location, several writers at once, converted to Iceberg in place; commits via iceberg-rust; per-table credential vending; HA on PostgreSQL; Cairn identities governed per table

Trino 484 on the lakehouse. Per-team warehouses that stop when idle and start on the first query (USE_WAREHOUSE); Cairn sign-in (JWT, OAuth2 SSO for the web UI and BI); access control through Cairn's policies (OPA protocol); query lineage and usage into Cairn; resource groups; fault-tolerant execution, spill and cache; workers with autoscaling

Data preview and SQL editor on Trino, with autocomplete from the tables the person may query; AI functions (USE_AI_FUNCTIONS) and inline Python functions in SQL; Ask-your-data (text-to-SQL) with the caller's permissions

dbt-core 1.12 with dbt-trino (cairn dbt, cairn/dbt). Runs as a pipeline user; docs, tags, owners, lineage and tests recorded in Cairn; Helm CronJobs. Derived tables: a SELECT kept as a table, refreshed fully, by watermark or by merge, on a schedule or when what it reads changes, as its owner
Apache Airflow 3.3 (cairn/airflow, cairn-airflow-provider). Cairn operators for Trino and dbt; OpenLineage to Cairn; UI sign-in through Cairn with group → role mapping; official chart values
Spark 4.0 with Iceberg 1.10 (cairn/spark, cairn-spark). Signed in as a Cairn identity; each table decided by Cairn; per-table credentials, read-only unless writable; column lineage to Cairn

Policy decision point (RBAC with ABAC, deny-overrides, obligations), masking on every read path, row filters, personas and purposes, PII classification and propagation, certification workflows, compliance forms, hash-chained audit log
Cairn Core: search, search by meaning, lineage (column level), glossary, domains, data products, change history, bulk editing, workspaces, i18n
Monitors (volume, freshness, schema, drift, learned thresholds), data contracts, profiling, incidents, results from dbt and other tools
Assistant, documentation drafts, context agents, governed metrics (semantic layer), MCP server, AI-system governance, usage and budgets; Claude or local models
Internal marketplace with access requests; publishing to Snowflake listings and Delta Sharing shares

Source connectors and in-VPC remote agents (signed, sealed); the store's message queues and events; pipes (files landing in the store, loaded once each); streams (Kafka and Debezium CDC into Iceberg, exactly once)

Compose and Helm (HA, network policies, PDBs); infrastructure as code (cairn bundle from git, a Terraform provider); SSO and SCIM; Alembic migrations; signed images with SBOMs; monitoring dashboards; hosting tenants, with a ready Hetzner setup (deploy/hetzner: k3s on dedicated servers, shared PostgreSQL with backups, per-tenant search and Kafka, tenant isolation, tested in CI)

items.title: Table maintenance service
items.summary: Snapshot expiry, orphan-file removal, data-file compaction and manifest rewrites per table, on a schedule and on demand, with retention as a table property
items.done: A table with 1,000 small files and 100 snapshots is compacted and expired on schedule. Time travel within retention still works, orphaned files are gone, and every action is audited
items.note: policies per table, schema or default; compaction, snapshot expiry, orphan removal on a schedule; automatic clustering: sort columns chosen from what the table's queries filter on (Trino's query history), the sort order set and the files rewritten when they overlap (tests/test_trino_e2e.py)

items.title: Governed Spark on restricted tables
items.summary: A policy-enforcing scan path for masks and row filters (Spark Connect on trusted compute, or a Cairn-planned scan through Trino), so Spark users are no longer refused
items.done: ana reads a masked table in Spark and sees masked values. bob's row filter returns only his rows. Neither can reach the raw files
items.note: a Cairn-planned scan through Trino: cairn_spark.governed_read reads as the user, with their masks and row filters, partitioned; the catalog still refuses the files (tests/test_spark_e2e.py)

items.title: Spark on Kubernetes
items.summary: Cluster-mode submission and Spark Operator SparkApplications with no secret in the cluster (the driver signs in by workload identity), CairnSparkApplicationOperator for Airflow, driver RBAC and a history server in the chart; then per-team namespaces with quotas
items.done: An Airflow DAG submits a Spark job to the cluster as a pipeline user. Its lineage and run appear in Cairn, and the job is refused a table outside its grants
items.note: submission, operator, Airflow task and history server (tests/test_spark_k8s_e2e.py); on a full cluster in CI (kind): a cluster-mode job's driver pod signs in with its projected service-account token, starts an executor pod, reads a governed table and is refused another (tests/test_spark_kind_e2e.py); per-team quotas (tests/test_spark_teams_k8s.py)

items.title: Notebooks
items.summary: JupyterHub with Cairn sign-in; kernels with cairn-spark and Trino as the signed-in person; notebooks as catalog assets
items.done: A person signs in through Cairn, queries Trino and Spark from a notebook under their own policies, and the notebook appears in Cairn with lineage
items.note: JupyterHub signs people in through Cairn (OAuth client jupyterhub); each person's server gets a Cairn token of their own, suspended with them; %%sql on Trino and %cairn spark as the person; saved notebooks become catalog assets owned by them with lineage from their %%sql tables (cairn_lakehouse.jupyter, helm/jupyterhub/values-cairn.yaml, tests/test_jupyterhub_e2e.py with a real JupyterHub)

items.title: Streaming and CDC ingestion
items.summary: Kafka → Iceberg (Kafka Connect Iceberg sink) and Debezium CDC as governed pipelines, with exactly-once commits and schema evolution
items.done: A PostgreSQL table's changes arrive in an Iceberg table within a minute, with lineage from the source and quality monitors on freshness
items.note: Kafka JSON and Debezium CDC into Iceberg (cairn streams): upserts and deletes, offsets in the table snapshots for exactly once, rejects, schema evolution, source lineage (tests/test_streams_e2e.py)

items.title: Workload management and chargeback
items.summary: Trino resource groups and Spark quotas per team, with costs from Trino and Spark query statistics fed into the cost report automatically
items.done: Two teams' queries are isolated under load, and each team's compute and storage costs appear per day without manual posting
items.note: resource groups and cost report exist; Spark compute is priced per application from its runs (CAIRN_COST_SPARK_USD_PER_CORE_HOUR); team warehouses scale to zero and their workers follow the load, with node-hours priced in the cost report (tests/test_warehouses_scaling_e2e.py); cost budgets per domain, owner, platform, tables, warehouse or AI, with threshold and forecast alerts once a period (tests/test_budgets.py); per-query Trino costs attributed to people, teams and tables (L60)

items.title: Machine learning
items.summary: MLflow tracking and model registry behind Cairn sign-in; models and features as catalog assets, with lineage from training tables
items.done: A model trained in Spark is registered as a pipeline user. Cairn shows its lineage to the training tables, and access to the model follows Cairn's policy
items.note: MLflow behind Cairn sign-in (/v1/ml): runs attributed to the caller, an owned and governed registry, versions in the catalog with lineage from training tables, serving through Cairn with USE_ML_MODEL (tests/test_ml_e2e.py, trained with scikit-learn); feature tables as catalog assets with their lineage, declared by the table's owners (tests/test_feature_tables.py); an online feature store: feature tables served by entity key, kept in step with the table's snapshots, each lookup governed as a read (masks as Trino applies them, row-filtered callers refused) (tests/test_online_features_e2e.py); model monitoring: every served call logged, drift (PSI) against the training table or a reference period, accuracy from labels, alerts on drift, payloads for the model's managers only (tests/test_ml_e2e.py, tests/test_model_monitoring_e2e.py); Spark training and serving deployments in the chart to do

items.title: Open data sharing
items.summary: Iceberg REST sharing to external recipients, with recipient identities, expiry and revocation in Cairn
items.done: A recipient in another organisation reads a shared table with pyiceberg. Revoking the share stops access at once
items.note: shares through Iceberg REST: recipient credential, only the shared tables, read-only scoped keys, expiry, revocation at once, never a masked or filtered table (/v1/shares, Pipelines → Shares, tests/test_shares_e2e.py); publishing to Snowflake and Delta Sharing; clean rooms: approved aggregate templates only, k-anonymous results, the room's own Trino identity reading only its tables (/v1/clean-rooms, tests/test_trino_e2e.py); differentially private rooms: Laplace noise on counts and clipped sums, an epsilon budget spent atomically and refused once used (tested on Trino); outside parties (partner:<name>) signing in with a secret shown once, uploading their data as a table only the room reads, proposing and running templates (tested on Trino with the real store and catalog)

items.title: Disaster recovery across regions
items.summary: Store replication, catalog and Cairn database replicas, and a tested failover runbook with measured recovery point and recovery time objectives
items.done: A region is lost in a test. The standby serves the lakehouse with the recorded RPO and RTO
items.note: standby store by bucket replication, standby PostgreSQL by streaming, a failover runbook and cairn dr reconcile (tables whose newest files never arrived move back to their newest whole commit); drill in CI with the primary region killed: RPO 4 of 10 commits (4.3 s), RTO about 2 s (tests/test_dr_drill.py); automatic failover (cairn dr watch): the standby databases promoted and DNS repointed by TSIG-signed RFC 2136 updates once the whole primary is lost and only onto a healthy standby, never failing back by itself; drilled with a real BIND server and Cairn's own database (audit chain whole, writes taken), DNS switched 1.4 s after the loss

items.title: Scale and assurance
items.summary: Load tests: PDP p99 under 5 ms cached at 2k rps, catalog decisions on 1k-table jobs, store throughput. Chaos tests. An external penetration test. KMS or HSM for gateway keys
items.done: Published results in CI, and pentest findings closed
items.note: in CI: cached decisions p99 0.02 ms at about 107k/s on one thread and a 1,000-table catalog decision in 0.6 s cold, 0.1 s warm (tests/test_scale_decisions.py, after indexing policies by privilege, compiling target patterns once and a cheaper cache key); chaos with a replica killed mid-commit, the database restarted and the store crashed, nothing acknowledged lost or doubled (catalog/conformance/test_chaos.py); every route refused to strangers but a reviewed public list, security headers (tests/test_route_security.py); KMS, Key Vault, Cloud KMS and KMIP HSMs for store keys (L22). An external penetration test, store throughput at scale and a KMS or HSM for gateway keys to do

items.title: Upgrade matrix
items.summary: Pin-and-test against new Trino, Iceberg, Spark, dbt and Airflow releases
items.done: A version bump is merged only after CI passes with the new engine version
items.note: deploy/versions/pins.json (checked against every file that pins), a weekly workflow that finds each engine's newest release and runs the matching end-to-end suites on it (cairn-upgrade-matrix.yml); tried here: Trino 484 needed two renamed settings, then passed all 21 Trino tests

items.title: Zero-copy clones, undrop, branches and tags
items.summary: Clone a table without copying its data; bring back a dropped table; write-audit-publish on Iceberg branches
items.done: A clone reads the source's files and writes its own; neither can expire what they share; a dropped table comes back within the retention, a purged one does not
items.note: POST …/tables/{t}/clone, …/undrop, GET …/dropped in Cairn Catalog; branches and tags kept by the catalog, tested with pyiceberg (catalog/conformance/test_clones.py)

items.title: HTTP streaming ingestion
items.summary: Producers post rows into lakehouse tables without Kafka, exactly once
items.done: A producer that retries a request writes nothing twice and resumes where the table says
items.note: http streams: POST /v1/ingest/<name>/rows with per-channel offsets in the table's snapshots, INGEST_STREAM (tests/test_ingest_http_e2e.py)

items.title: Query insight
items.summary: Query history, profiles and tuning hints
items.done: A person sees their own slow queries with why they were slow; operators see all
items.note: /v1/queries from Trino's events: per-query statistics and SQL for its author and operators, hints for queueing, wide or unfiltered reads, cross joins, unbounded sorts, memory and failures (tests/test_trino_e2e.py); a Query insight page with filters and profiles (tests/test_sql_ops_ui_e2e.py, in Chromium)

items.title: Files as data
items.summary: Directory tables and document text extraction
items.done: A folder of documents is a table with each file's text, kept current as files change
items.note: files pipes: one row per object with its metadata and the text of text, HTML, PDF, Word and PowerPoint files, updated on change and removed on delete; scanned PDF pages and images read by OCR (Tesseract, in Cairn's image), with per-page and per-document limits reported on the row (tests/test_pipes_e2e.py)

items.title: Vector search on lakehouse data
items.summary: Search a table's text by meaning, governed
items.done: A question finds the right rows; an index follows its table; only readers search it
items.note: vector indexes: chunks embedded with the deployment's model into <table>__<index>_vectors, one per index, refreshed incrementally, searched with READ on the source and never past a mask or row filter (tests/test_vectors_e2e.py); approximate (ANN) indexes for very large tables to do; approximate search (IVF: k-means lists trained at refresh, stored beside the vectors, the nearest lists searched; exact when the stored index is not for the current snapshot), recall@10 1.0 at a tenth of the work in tests

items.title: Scheduled SQL and in-product workflows
items.summary: Steps that depend on each other, on a schedule, as their owner
items.done: A nightly refresh, a check and a report run in order; a failed check stops what follows and tells the owner
items.note: SQL workflows (/v1/sql-workflows): derived refreshes, checks and reports in a DAG on cron, with retries, run history and notifications (tests/test_sql_workspace.py, tests/test_trino_e2e.py); a SQL workflows page with a step editor, Run now and run history (tests/test_sql_ops_ui_e2e.py, in Chromium)

items.title: Infrastructure as code for SQL and search
items.summary: Saved queries, dashboards, alerts, SQL workflows and vector indexes in bundles and Terraform; Terraform data sources
items.done: A team keeps its reports in git: a plan shows only real changes, and references between them stay right
items.note: bundle kinds and Terraform resources for all five, references by name (bundles) or id (Terraform), subset drift checks, one data source per type (tests/test_bundles.py, tests/test_terraform_provider.py with Terraform 1.13); policies (one at a time, serialized, audited) and connections as bundle kinds and Terraform resources, with data sources (tests/test_bundles.py, tests/test_policy_items.py, tests/test_terraform_provider.py); warehouses stay deployment config, their access a policy; a registry-ready release (GoReleaser, signed checksums, manifest) checked in CI. Publishing to the public registry needs the provider's own repository and a GPG key

items.title: Delta Lake beyond one writer, and into Iceberg
items.summary: Concurrent Delta writers on Cairn Store; Delta tables converted to Iceberg without copying
items.done: Two clusters write one Delta table at once and lose nothing; a Delta table becomes an Iceberg table in place
items.note: conditional-write commits (s3.exclusive-create, checked atomically by Cairn Store), proven with two Trino clusters; in-place conversion from the Delta log (checkpoints and commits), refusing partitioned tables, deletion vectors and column mapping (tests/test_trino_e2e.py); converting partitioned tables and deletion vectors in place to do; partitioned tables (partition values from the log, identity partitions) and deletion vectors (decoded, only those files rewritten) convert too, tested on tables Trino wrote

items.title: Git-backed SQL and notebooks
items.summary: Saved queries and notebooks kept in a git repository, pulled and pushed by their owner
items.done: A team reviews its queries in pull requests; a merged change reaches Cairn, and an edit made in Cairn is proposed back
items.note: Git folders over the git command (any host): pull to saved queries and catalog notebooks, conflicts reported rather than overwritten, push to a new branch with a pull request for configured hosts (tests/test_git_folders.py); a Git folders page to link, pull (conflicts shown) and push (tests/test_sql_ops_ui_e2e.py, in Chromium); notebooks round-trip through JupyterHub: a folder's notebooks are synced into each owner's server, saves there are pushed (outputs cleared), conflicts reported and local work never overwritten (tests/test_jupyterhub_e2e.py, real JupyterHub and git)

items.title: Stored functions and procedures
items.summary: SQL and Python functions kept in a catalog; parameterized procedures
items.done: A team shares a function everyone may call under policy; an operator gives a few people a procedure for a controlled change
items.note: stored functions in a routines catalog, USE_FUNCTION per function with masks applied first; procedures with typed, bound parameters run as the caller, EXECUTE_PROCEDURE per procedure (tests/test_trino_e2e.py); owner's-rights procedures deliberately not offered; functions as catalog assets: published from Trino's events (creator as owner, signatures, body, comment, overloads and drops), a sync for what was missed, the policy's function urn on the asset (tests/test_trino_e2e.py, tests/test_trino_functions.py)

items.title: Customer keys beyond Vault
items.summary: Customer-managed keys in AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Google Cloud KMS and KMIP HSMs for Cairn Store
items.done: A customer disables their key and their objects can no longer be read
items.note: aws-kms external keys: SigV4, the object's name as the encryption context, rotated credentials picked up (store/conformance/test_kms_aws.py against a real KMS-compatible server). ✅ azure-keyvault (RSA-OAEP-256 wrap, the wrapping version kept, client secret, workload identity, managed identity), gcp-kms (the object's name as AAD, signed service-account sign-in or the metadata server) and kmip (KMIP 1.4 over mutual TLS, AES-GCM in the HSM), tested against Lowkey Vault, floci-gcp and PyKMIP's server, with a disabled version, a key the object was not written with, a refused certificate and a revoked key (store/conformance/test_kms_cloud.py)

items.title: Data apps
items.summary: Streamlit and other web apps served by Cairn, each viewer signed in and governed as themselves
items.done: A team ships an app; people open it with their Cairn sign-in and see only their own data
items.note: /apps/<name>/ proxy (HTTP and WebSocket), USE_APP per app, the viewer's identity and a Trino token for them passed to the app, forged headers stripped, apps started on demand and stopped when idle (tests/test_data_apps_e2e.py, Streamlit in Chromium); apps from git at a deployed commit (tests/test_data_apps_git.py); a Kubernetes runtime: a Deployment per app at the deployed commit, started on a visit and stopped when idle, locked-down pods reached only by Cairn, the chart's namespace Role (tests/test_data_apps_k8s.py on kind)

items.title: Materialized views
items.summary: A query's result kept as a table and refreshed when what it reads changes, written in SQL
items.done: An analyst writes CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW; any write to its source, from any engine, refreshes it, and it says when it is stale
items.note: CREATE, REFRESH and DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW in the SQL editor, refreshed on change as their owner, fresh/stale with what changed; Cairn Catalog reports every commit, so pyiceberg, Spark and Trino writes all count (tests/test_trino_e2e.py, tests/test_lakehouse_client_e2e.py)

items.title: Change data feed
items.summary: A table's row changes since a snapshot, for consumers that sync or react
items.done: A downstream system reads only what changed since it last looked, seeing what its reader may see
items.note: GET /v1/lakehouse/tables/<schema>/<table>/changes (inserts, deletes, updates by key, the next cursor) and .../snapshots, read as the caller so masks and row filters apply; Iceberg metadata tables decided on their table (value-bearing ones for its managers), and connector table functions that bypass masks (table_changes, JDBC query) for operators only (tests/test_trino_e2e.py, tests/test_trino_access.py)

items.title: SIEM export
items.summary: The audit log pushed to Splunk HEC, syslog (RFC 5424 and CEF, over TLS) and HTTPS sinks as it is written
items.done: A security team's SIEM holds every audit entry in order and can verify the chain; a sink that is down loses nothing
items.note: at-least-once, ordered delivery with a cursor per sink, backoff, lease and rewind; tokens from files; tested against Vector as the receiver (tests/test_siem_e2e.py)

items.title: Signup and billing
items.summary: Self-service signup, Stripe Checkout and a tenant whose licence follows its subscription
items.done: A team signs up, pays and gets its workspace; renewals extend its licence, a cancelled one turns read-only after its grace with its data kept
items.note: email confirmation, Checkout, signed and idempotent webhooks, provisioning through tenant.sh with retries, renewals and plan changes reissuing the licence, the billing portal by emailed link (tests/test_signup_e2e.py, against stripe-mock and Mailpit)

items.title: Usage metering

items.done: A tenant's Trino CPU, warehouse time and AI spend appear on its invoice, each day billed once
items.note: signed daily reports with per-tenant keys derived on the control plane, delivered by tenant.sh --metering-key and the chart; settled days sent as Stripe meter events with idempotent identifiers (tests/test_metering_e2e.py, against stripe-mock)

items.title: Status page
items.summary: Components probed, 90-day uptime, incidents and maintenance, public
items.done: Customers see when a part of the platform is down or degraded, and what operators say about it
items.note: probes with operational/degraded/outage, daily uptime, incidents with updates and scheduled maintenance, a script-free page, JSON and an Atom feed (tests/test_status_page_e2e.py, against a real Cairn Store stopped and restarted)

items.title: Gateway API

items.done: A cluster without ingress-nginx serves Cairn through its Gateway with the same paths
items.note: core.gateway in the chart, the same routing as the Ingress (prefix rewrites, X-Forwarded-Prefix, timeouts, consoles blocked), validated against the Gateway API schemas; tenant.sh on a shared Gateway (CAIRN_GATEWAY); the end-to-end check through Envoy Gateway on kind (tests/test_gateway_api_kind.py) runs in CI's kind job

items.title: BI: spreadsheet workbooks
items.summary: Explore a table like a spreadsheet: formulas, filters, grouping, pivots, compiled to SQL and run as the viewer
items.done: An analyst builds revenue by region and quarter without SQL; a colleague with masked columns sees them masked
items.note: the formula language compiled safely to Trino SQL, workbook elements with calculated columns, row and group filters, aggregates and pivots, saved and shared workbooks, the Workbooks page (tests/test_workbooks.py, tests/test_trino_e2e.py, tests/test_sql_ops_ui_e2e.py)

items.title: BI: input tables (writeback)

items.done: Finance types quarterly targets next to actuals; a workbook compares them at once; a stale edit never overwrites a colleague's
items.note: create, add, edit and delete rows as the person (Trino asks Cairn for each statement), typed literals, optimistic concurrency on _updated_at, catalog registration, audit, the Input tables page (tests/test_trino_e2e.py, tests/test_input_tables.py, inputTables.test.tsx)

items.title: BI: interactive dashboards

items.done: A sales lead picks EU and a date range, clicks a region to filter the orders, drills from region to country; each viewer still sees only their rows

items.title: BI: metrics layer

items.done: Each outage fails closed and recovers without lost writes
items.note: PDP and catalog stopped under Trino load, gateway restarted and Core refusing writes mid-run; Core itself at its edge (buffers and outboxes)

items.title: SAML single sign-on
items.summary: SAML 2.0 alongside OIDC: SP metadata, signed assertions checked, groups from attributes
items.done: An Okta/ADFS/Entra tenant set up for SAML signs people in to Cairn with their groups; a forged or replayed assertion is refused
items.note: Cairn as SAML service provider (signed response or assertion, signature-wrapping and replay refused, audience, recipient, validity, InResponseTo) and OpenID provider for Cairn Core (code + PKCE, own signing key, groups claim); audited (tests/test_saml_e2e.py against Keycloak)

items.title: Secrets for people's notebooks and jobs
items.summary: Secret scopes owned by people or groups, read by notebooks, workflows and Spark as the person
items.done: A notebook reads an API key from a scope its user may read; nobody else can; the value is never logged or shown again

items.title: Sharing BI assets with people and groups
items.summary: Viewer and editor roles on dashboards, workbooks and saved queries (metrics stay platform-wide definitions)
items.done: A dashboard shared with Finance as viewers opens for Finance only; an editor changes it; others get 404

items.title: Retention enforced, legal hold and automated erasure
items.summary: Retention policies delete expired rows; legal hold blocks deletes and expiry on a table; right-to-be-forgotten deletes rows and proves it
items.done: Rows older than the policy are gone after the run; a table on hold keeps them; an erasure request ends with a signed report of rows removed

items.title: Per-tenant and per-user API quotas, and tenant IP allowlists
items.done: A user over their quota gets 429 with Retry-After; a request from outside the tenant's allowlist is refused

items.title: BI folders, comments and usage analytics
items.done: Dashboards organised in folders, discussed in threads, and a report shows who uses which and which are stale
items.note: API and screens (folders, threads, usage and stale assets), tested in Chromium

items.title: Metric alerts
items.summary: Thresholds and anomaly detection on metrics
items.done: Revenue dropping 20% week over week, or out of its usual range, notifies the owner once
items.note: Change, range and threshold rules per period, run as the owner, told once per change of state; tested on Trino

items.title: Map and heatmap charts; dashboards that work on a phone
items.done: A region map and a heatmap render from metric tiles; a dashboard is usable at phone width
items.note: Heatmap and point-map charts (operator's tiles optional); one-column dashboards on a phone, tested in Chromium as an iPhone

items.title: Export files delivered to Slack and Teams
items.done: A scheduled export arrives in a Slack channel as a file, each recipient's own view
items.note: Each recipient's own copy uploaded to their Slack DM; Teams gets a link to it (webhooks carry no files); shared channels are told but never given a copy

items.title: Metrics over SQL for outside BI tools
items.done: Tableau or Power BI queries a metric through Trino as the signed-in person and gets the same number as the dashboard
items.note: Metrics published as SECURITY INVOKER views read on their table's terms; same numbers as Cairn's metric query per person, tested on Trino (summable measures only)

items.title: Scheduled notebook and Python jobs in Cairn
items.done: A notebook runs nightly as its owner, its output kept, failures notified
items.note: Notebooks and scripts on a cron, each run in a locked-down container (Docker) or a Kubernetes Job, with a Trino token for its owner; output and log kept, failures told; tested with the real image on Docker, Trino (row filters) and kind

items.title: Governed volumes
items.summary: Folders of files under Cairn's policies, not only S3 policies
items.done: A volume shared with a group is readable by them alone, through the API and Spark
items.note: Volumes (a bucket each) under Cairn's grants to people and groups; files through the API, and narrowed, short-lived store credentials for Spark; tested on a real store and in Spark (CI)

items.title: Snapshot browser and restore
items.done: A person sees a table's snapshots and restores yesterday's, audited
items.note: Snapshots tab with row counts, the table as it was (as the person sees it), and restore with a reason, as the person on Trino (MANAGE_DATASET), audited and undoable; tested on Trino and in the UI

items.title: Cost per query, user and table on Trino
items.done: The cost report attributes Trino CPU and scanned bytes to people, teams and tables
items.note: Each query priced from its CPU and scanned bytes; attributed to people, teams (even split) and tables (even split), in the table cost report, on query profiles and a Reports tab; people see their own; tested on Trino and in the UI

items.title: SaaS data connectors
items.summary: Loading from Salesforce, HubSpot and similar into Iceberg
items.done: Salesforce accounts land in a governed table on a schedule, incrementally
items.note: Salesforce and HubSpot into Iceberg on a cron, incremental by modification time, upserted by id, keys from secret scopes as the owner, WRITE_DATASET checked each run; Google Sheets loaded whole each run (service account JWT or API key); Excel workbooks through file pipes (format: xlsx, typed columns), tested with real files, store and catalog; Salesforce, HubSpot and Sheets tested end to end against an emulated API (not yet against a real org or Google account)

items.title: Reverse ETL
items.summary: Syncing governed tables out to SaaS apps
items.done: A segment table syncs to a CRM as its owner; masked columns are never sent
items.note: HubSpot and Salesforce upserts read on Trino as the owner (row filters apply), refused when a sent column is masked for them, EXPORT_DATASET checked each run, only changed rows sent, rejects retried; tested on Trino against an emulated API (not yet a real account)

items.title: Managed model serving
items.summary: Deployments with autoscaling from the registry
items.done: A registered model is deployed from Cairn, scales with load and is invoked as the caller
items.note: Deployments of registered versions, invoked as the caller (USE_ML_MODEL), scaled by in-flight concurrency with scale-to-zero, on MLflow's model server as local processes or, in the chart, as a Deployment per model on Kubernetes (Cairn's Role, network policy, no credentials in the pods); tested with real MLflow, and on a kind cluster in CI (run 287)

items.title: Build and deploy custom agents
items.done: A team defines an agent with tools and scopes, deploys it, and its actions are governed and traced
items.note: Agents built from the assistant's tools with scopes (read, query_data, propose), deployed with draft-on-change, run as the caller narrowed to their tools and scopes, under the pause switch, quotas, AI budget and AI system approval, traced and audited; tested on real services with a scripted model, not yet against a live model

items.title: SDKs beyond Python, and an API deprecation policy
items.done: JS and Java clients for the main APIs; deprecated routes send Deprecation and Sunset headers
items.note: Dependency-free JavaScript/TypeScript and Java 17 clients for the main APIs (identity, health, search and questions, governed SQL, saved queries, products and access requests, custom agents), tested over HTTP against a real Cairn API (governed answers, bearer tokens, agent keys, retries, deprecation warnings); deprecated routes send Deprecation, Sunset and successor Link headers, are marked in the OpenAPI document and answer 410 after their sunset (180 days minimum notice)

items.title: Consent management
items.done: A subject's withdrawn consent excludes their rows from purposes that need it
items.note: Purposes that need consent (opt-out or opt-in, members by user, group or persona, an identifier kind); records kept only as hashes; members' queries exclude withdrawn subjects on Trino (row filters) and on direct connections (query rewrite), failing closed; tested on real Trino, PostgreSQL and SQLite. Policy row filters now apply on direct connections too

items.title: Accessibility tested
items.summary: Automated axe checks of the main pages in CI
items.done: The main pages pass axe with no serious violations
items.note: Twenty main pages checked with axe-core (WCAG 2.1 A/AA) in Chromium against a running Cairn, in CI; fixed what it found: antd Select's closed-combobox ARIA (corrected at build), the SQL editor's textbox ARIA, unnamed progress bars and an unlabelled input; dialogs and other opened states are not covered yet

items.title: Failover for tenant OpenSearch and Kafka
items.summary: Replicated tenant services: three-node OpenSearch and three Kafka brokers (KRaft quorum), spread over nodes with disruption budgets
items.done: A tenant keeps searching and its events keep flowing when it loses a node; writes that could be lost are refused
items.note: CAIRN_TENANT_SERVICES_HA=1. Tested on the rendered manifest in Docker: Kafka with a broker lost (no write lost or stopped) and two lost (writes refused); OpenSearch with a node lost (every document readable, writes go on, green again when it rejoins). Tested on k3s (deploy/hetzner/ci/k3s-smoke.sh, CI run 286): the release reaches each broker by name through the policy, an OpenSearch pod and a broker deleted lose nothing

items.title: Spark training and model serving in the chart
items.summary: Model deployments as Kubernetes Deployments scaled by Cairn; Spark training tracked in MLflow through Cairn as the job
items.done: A team trains on Spark as its pipeline user, registers the model, deploys it from Cairn and it scales on the cluster
items.note: Model serving on Kubernetes tested on kind in CI (run 287: a Deployment per model deployment with only the chart's Role, scaled from zero by traffic and back, refused to people without the model's rights, no credentials in pods). Spark training: cairn_spark.mlflow tested with real MLflow through Cairn (the job tracked as its user, with lineage); pyspark.ml training in the cairn/spark image (spark-submit), registered through Cairn as the job's user with the table as lineage, green in CI run 288

items.title: Sample datasets for new tenants
items.summary: A documented retail lakehouse (customers, products, orders) with starter queries
items.done: A new tenant explores search, SQL and dashboards on real tables before its own data arrives
items.note: /v1/samples, cairn samples, loaded once on a new tenant's first start (CAIRN_TENANT_SAMPLES, chart cairn.samples.onStart), never back after a removal; tested with the real store, catalog and Trino (tests/test_trino_e2e.py)

items.title: Access reviews
items.summary: Recertification campaigns over the access people hold
items.done: Owners confirm or revoke each grant by a due date; what nobody vouches for is taken away; auditors get the record
items.note: /governance/access-reviews: product owners review request-based grants, no self-review, revoke at once, undecided revoked at the due date (or kept), reminders, audited; tested on SQLite and PostgreSQL with the real PDP (tests/test_access_reviews.py)

items.title: Bad-row quarantine in pipes and streams
items.summary: Rows a table refuses are set aside instead of failing the load
items.done: One bad value no longer stops a file or a stream; the bad rows are kept, with the reason, to fix and reload
items.note: bad_rows: quarantine on pipes and streams; set-aside rows with file and row (or offset), reason and value (/v1/pipes/{id}/rejects, /v1/streams/{id}/rejects); upserts leave the refused key alone; tested with the real store and catalog (tests/test_pipes_e2e.py, tests/test_streams_e2e.py)

items.title: Data residency
items.summary: Lakehouse namespaces pinned to a region
items.done: Regulated data stays in its region: stored there, processed only by deployments the pin allows, sent only to allowed regions; even an administrator cannot move it by a setting
items.note: Rules file shared by Cairn and Cairn Catalog (cairn.residency in the chart). The catalog keeps pinned tables in their region's location (create, register, commit, write.*.path, clone, rename, namespace location), refusing an administrator too. Trino and lakehouse engines read pinned tables only in an allowed CAIRN_REGION; shares and reverse syncs need an allowed destination region. Tested with the real store, catalog and Cairn (tests/test_residency_e2e.py). Not yet: copies made by SQL into unpinned namespaces are not followed (lineage shows them); store bucket replication targets are not checked

items.title: Reversible tokenisation
items.summary: Sensitive values replaced by tokens where data lands, given back only to people allowed to
items.done: The lakehouse, shares, exports and copies hold tokens, never the values; joins still work; erasure by forgetting
items.note: Token domains with their own keys (wrapped by CAIRN_TOKENS_KEY, rotatable without changing tokens); deterministic keyed tokens; an encrypted vault; TOKENIZE/DETOKENIZE by policy, a required purpose, audited without values; forgetting values or tokens; pipes and streams tokenise columns (upsert keys too). Tested on SQLite and PostgreSQL with the real PDP (tests/test_tokens.py) and with the real store and catalog (tests/test_pipes_e2e.py, tests/test_streams_e2e.py)

items.title: Table branches, tags and data diff
items.summary: Iceberg refs under Cairn's policies, write-audit-publish, and a diff of any two versions
items.done: Pipelines write to a branch, checks gate the publish, and reviewers see exactly what changed, under their own masks
items.note: /v1/tables/{t}/refs (branches, tags, MANAGE_DATASET), publish with SQL checks on the branch as the caller and a fast-forward of main (refused when main moved on), /v1/tables/{t}/diff (schema; rows added, removed and changed by key, or EXCEPT ALL) on Trino as the caller; audited. Tested on real Trino and Cairn Catalog (tests/test_trino_e2e.py)

items.title: Synthetic test data
items.summary: A table shaped like a real one, with none of its people
items.done: Development, tests and demos get realistic data without a copy of production
items.note: /v1/synthetic: statistics on Trino as the caller (their masks apply); sensitive and masked columns made from type and shape alone, without their extremes; categories only when common (k ≥ 10); nulls, distributions, ranges, lengths and uniqueness kept; seeded, marked and audited. Tested on real Trino and Cairn Catalog (tests/test_trino_e2e.py)

items.title: Speech to text for audio and video files
items.summary: Recordings in a files pipe become searchable text
items.done: Calls, meetings and voice notes join documents in SQL, search and AI, without leaving the deployment
items.note: Local Whisper (faster-whisper, the media extra): text and length in seconds on the files table; models put in place beforehand (cairn transcribe-model download, never downloaded while loading), one process per file with a time limit and a length limit read from the header, no network. Tested with the real store and catalog (tests/test_pipes_e2e.py)

items.title: AI enrichment of files: image description and field extraction
items.summary: The model describes images and pulls named fields out of documents as they land
items.done: Invoices, forms, photos and scans become columns you can query, like Snowflake's AI_EXTRACT and image AI functions
items.note: Files pipes' ai: description, labels and extracted (JSON) columns, ai_error on failure; images scaled and sent as JPEG under the OCR pixel limit; Cairn's metered model (Anthropic or local Ollama), charged to the pipe's owner. Tested with the real store and catalog (tests/test_pipes_e2e.py) and per provider (tests/test_llm_images.py)

items.title: Governed geospatial
items.summary: Location data under policy, spatial SQL on it
items.done: Analysts map and measure where things happen without seeing exact addresses; the equivalent of Snowflake's GEOGRAPHY governance
items.note: geo mask strategy: coordinates rounded (CAIRN_GEO_MASK_DECIMALS), WKT/Geometry/SphericalGeography reduced to a rounded centre, partial for other values; ranks above partial; location columns classified (PII.Location) by name and value; Trino's spatial functions on the coarse values; Policy Studio option. Tested on Trino (tests/test_trino_e2e.py) and in tests/test_geo_mask.py

items.title: Chargeback statements
items.summary: The month's bill per cost centre, from every cost Cairn knows
items.done: Finance charges teams for what they used: SQL, AI, storage, compute and runs, reconciled to the total
items.note: Cost centres (code, name, teams); SQL by who ran it, AI by who asked, tables by their owners, unattached runs by their owner; an unallocated line with reasons so the total reconciles; preview, frozen versioned statements, audited, CSV; members see their own lines. Tested on SQLite and PostgreSQL (tests/test_chargeback.py)

items.title: Point-lookup acceleration
items.summary: Bloom filters on the columns queries look rows up by
items.done: Lookups by order number, UUID or e-mail skip the files that cannot hold the value; Cairn's counterpart to Snowflake's search optimization
items.note: Maintenance policies' lookup: auto from Trino's query history (literal =/IN lookups, ≥10% of queries) or a list; parquet_bloom_filter_columns set and the files rewritten once; exact-value types only. Tested on real Trino (tests/test_trino_e2e.py): a miss inside min/max scans 0 rows against all rows unfiltered

items.title: Security posture scan
items.summary: Cairn checks its own configuration for the mistakes that expose data
items.done: Operators see, daily, what to fix first; the counterpart of Snowflake's Trust Center
items.note: Ten checks (trusted header, open policies, audit chain, unmasked PII, residency region, authz mode, long and idle shares, access reviews, secrets key, AI budget) with severity, evidence and fix; a score; daily scans kept with history; new high findings sent to CAIRN_SECURITY_CONTACTS; a failing check reported, never passed. Tested with real components (tests/test_posture.py)

items.title: Passkeys and step-up
items.summary: A fresh passkey check before the most sensitive actions
items.done: Detokenising, forgetting tokens and sharing outside need the person's own device, whatever the sign-in was; phishing-resistant
items.note: WebAuthn registration and assertions (webauthn), step-up tokens (5 minutes, the person only, hashed), X-Cairn-Step-Up on the listed actions (CAIRN_STEP_UP_ACTIONS), new passkeys only with an existing one, one-use challenges, origin and counter checks; audited. Tested over HTTP with a software authenticator (tests/test_passkeys.py). Sign-in MFA itself stays with the identity provider

items.title: The assistant's memory, artifacts and deep research
items.summary: Notes kept per person, outputs saved and shared, questions researched in steps
items.done: People pick up where they left off, keep and share what the assistant made, and get a cited report for a broad question; the counterpart of Snowflake Intelligence's memory, artifacts and deep research
items.note: Memory notes (saved only when asked; listed, deletable, switchable off; PII redacted; instruction-like notes refused; given to the model as data). Versioned artifacts that remember their source datasets: shared readers need access to every source at read time (fail closed). Deep research: plan, read-only steps as the asker, report artifact; cancel, budget stop, recovery after restart; audited. Tested with the real services, PDP, database and API and a scripted model (tests/test_ai_workspace.py)

items.title: Aggregation and projection policies
items.summary: Tables read only in aggregate, with a minimum group size; columns used but never returned
items.done: Pay, health or survey data can be analysed without anyone seeing a row; join and filter keys stay usable but hidden; the counterpart of Snowflake's aggregation and projection policies
items.note: Policy obligations (aggregation: min_group, entity_key; projection: columns). Cairn checks each query block that reads the table (no *, windows or ungrouped columns; protected columns never returned) and adds the HAVING floor, counting distinct entities when keyed; on Trino it runs as a one-query checked- identity with the person's row filters and masks, and direct Trino reads of such tables or columns are refused. Tested on SQLite results (tests/test_aggregation_policy.py) and on real Trino (test_aggregation_and_projection_policies_hold_on_trino)

items.title: Iceberg v3 tables
items.summary: Deletion vectors, row lineage, VARIANT and nanosecond timestamps, read and written by every engine Cairn ships
items.done: Spark 4, Trino and Cairn's own writers read and write the current Iceberg format through Cairn's catalog, and v2 tables upgrade in place; the counterpart of Snowflake's Iceberg v3 support (GA)
items.note: Catalog on iceberg-rust 0.11 (v3 types and metadata); Spark 4 / Iceberg 1.10 writes v3 with deletion vectors, row lineage and VARIANT and upgrades v2 tables; Trino pinned to 484 (Iceberg 1.12) reads deletion vectors and VARIANT and writes v3 (deletes as deletion vectors); Cairn's pyiceberg writers write v3 with row lineage (cairn.pipelines.iceberg_v3). Tested with real Spark, Trino 484 and pyiceberg on the store and catalog (catalog/conformance/test_iceberg_v3.py, tests/test_iceberg_v3_writes.py); the full Trino suite passes on 484. Rows kept by a pyiceberg rewrite take new row ids

items.title: Adaptive warehouses
items.summary: One endpoint that picks the warehouse size for each query
items.done: Nobody sizes a warehouse: heavy reports get the large one, everything else the small one, and a busy small one overflows; the counterpart of Snowflake's adaptive compute
items.note: Query fingerprints in query history (migration 0113) and POST /v1/warehouses/hint (median CPU, bytes, memory of earlier runs, behind the Trino key); the proxy routes each new query by that history or by load, keeps its follow-ups on the same tier, and shows where queries went; Helm warehouses.adaptive. Tested with two real Trino warehouses (tests/test_warehouses_adaptive_e2e.py)

items.title: Operational databases
items.summary: PostgreSQL databases for applications, made through Cairn and reached only with short-lived logins
items.done: Teams get a transactional database next to the lakehouse without a DBA ticket, and nobody holds a standing password; the counterpart of Snowflake Postgres and Databricks Lakebase (part 1: databases, logins, branches)
items.note: /v1/databases: create, branch (a copy with its own roles), drop; per-person logins (write/read, up to a day, dropped on expiry or revoke with their sessions), governed by CREATE_DATABASE, USE_DATABASE, VIEW_DATABASE, MANAGE_DATABASE; passwords never stored or audited; Helm cairn.databases. Tested on real PostgreSQL 16 (tests/test_databases.py). Mirroring into the lakehouse is part 2

items.title: Mirrors
items.summary: PostgreSQL tables kept in lakehouse tables through logical replication
items.done: Operational data reaches the lakehouse in seconds without running Kafka and Debezium; the counterpart of Snowflake's and Databricks' Postgres mirroring (part 2 of Postgres)
items.note: /v1/mirrors: a publication and a pgoutput slot per mirror, an initial copy, whole transactions per Iceberg commit through the streams writer, the slot advanced only after the commit (exactly once across crashes), upserts/deletes/key changes/truncate/new columns/TOAST, WAL retention shown, pause/resume/delete (slot and publication dropped). Tested with PostgreSQL 16 and the real store and catalog (tests/test_mirror_e2e.py)

items.title: App packages
items.summary: Data apps one team publishes and others install on their own data, with consent
items.done: A team ships an app once; others run it on their tables without handing over more than they bind; the counterpart of Snowflake Native Apps
items.note: Packages from git with immutable versions (commit + cairn-app.json manifest declaring read references); installs bind references to the installer's datasets (only ones they can read), run pinned to the commit with a minimal environment, and query Trino as cairnapp-<install>: the bound tables only, as the installer (masks, filters), read-only; upgrade/rollback rebinding; audited. Tested with real git and app processes (tests/test_app_packages.py) and on real Trino

items.title: Fine-tuning on governed data
items.summary: A language model tuned on examples read as the asker, trained and served in Cairn
items.done: Teams adapt a model to their tickets, products or wording without exporting data or holding a provider key; the counterpart of Cortex Fine-tuning
items.note: /v1/ml/finetunes: training sets from Cairn's governed query path (masks, filters, query policies), PII redacted, sources recorded; LoRA or full fine-tuning in an offline, isolated worker on PyTorch; per-epoch loss; generation behind USE_FINETUNE, audited without prompts; cairn finetune-model download. Tested with real LoRA training on PyTorch CPU (tests/test_finetune.py, ml job). GPU nodes and provider fine-tuning APIs are not covered

items.title: Connectors: MySQL change data capture
items.summary: MySQL tables mirrored into the lakehouse from the binary log
items.done: The second operational database family arrives change by change without Kafka or Debezium; the counterpart of Openflow's and Lakeflow's MySQL connectors
items.note: Mirrors accept mysql:// connections: settings checked (row-based log, full row image and metadata), a copy from a recorded log position, whole transactions (rolled-back ones leave nothing), key changes, deletes, TRUNCATE, log positions as offsets so a replay writes nothing twice, a purged position reported. Tested with MySQL 8.4 and the real store and catalog (tests/test_mirror_mysql_e2e.py). SQL Server and MongoDB follow (L96, L97); Oracle is not covered

items.title: Semantic model autopilot
items.summary: A draft semantic model built from tables and how they are queried, reviewed and published as metrics
items.done: Nobody writes a semantic model by hand: measures, filters, dimensions, a time column, relationships and synonyms come from the data and its use, checked as the person; the counterpart of Snowflake's Semantic View Autopilot
items.note: /sql/semantic-models (migration 0118): profiles as the person (masks and row filters apply), query history's shapes (aggregates with their filters, group-bys, joins) with no SQL text kept, filter values only when the person can read them, the model naming candidates by id only, every proposal run as the person, accepted ones saved as their metrics with synonyms (Ask-your-data and the AI builder use them). Tested on real Trino with history from its event listener and a scripted model (tests/test_trino_e2e.py)

items.title: Pipeline agent
items.summary: An agent that writes, tries, fixes and ships pipelines from a goal, as the person
items.done: "Revenue per region from paid orders" becomes a checked, scheduled derived table; a broken one is fixed from its failed runs; nothing ships without the person's approval; the counterpart of Snowflake's CoCo
items.note: /v1/pipeline-agent/tasks (migration 0119): the model proposes a derived table and checks (never sees rows); each try is planned, previewed and checked on Trino as the person, writing nothing, failures fed back (3 tries); approval creates or updates the derived table as theirs, refreshes it and checks the result; the pipeline returned as a bundle resource. Tested on real Trino with a scripted model (tests/test_trino_e2e.py); 🟡 not yet against a live model

items.title: CoWork: scheduled tasks and an approved outbox
items.summary: The assistant works for a person on a schedule and sends to Slack or email only once they approve
items.done: "Every Monday, summarise last week's orders" runs as its owner and lands in their artifacts; sending it to #sales waits for their click, and data they may not export never leaves; the counterpart of Snowflake's CoWork
items.note: /ai/scheduled-tasks and /ai/outbox (migration 0120): cron at most hourly, research runs as the owner (read-only tools, their budget), notifications with Send/Don't send buttons, targets only from operator allow-lists, approval re-checks EXPORT_DATASET on every source and redacts PII, expiry, suspended owners paused. Tested with Mailpit, a Slack Web API stand-in and a scripted model (tests/test_cowork.py); 🟡 not yet against a live model or Slack workspace

items.title: Connectors: SQL Server change data capture
items.summary: SQL Server tables mirrored into the lakehouse through CDC
items.done: The Microsoft operational databases arrive change by change without Debezium; the counterpart of Openflow's SQL Server connector
items.note: Mirrors accept mssql:// connections: CDC and a primary key checked (refused with the commands to run), a copy from the highest captured LSN (or the capture instance's start), whole transactions in commit order with old values for key changes, LSNs as offsets, purged changes reported. Tested with SQL Server 2022 and the real store and catalog (tests/test_mirror_mssql_e2e.py)

items.title: Connectors: MongoDB change streams
items.summary: MongoDB collections mirrored into the lakehouse
items.done: Document data arrives change by change, one row per document, new fields as new columns; the counterpart of Openflow's MongoDB connector
items.note: Mirrors accept mongodb:// connections (migration 0121 widens positions for resume tokens): replica set and collection checked, a copy from the cluster's operation time, inserts, updates (current document), replacements and deletes keyed by _id, transactions whole, resume tokens as positions, a dropped collection or lost oplog reported. Tested with MongoDB 7 and the real store and catalog (tests/test_mirror_mongo_e2e.py)

items.title: Document sources: SharePoint and Google Drive
items.summary: Folders kept in a store prefix and indexed by a files pipe
items.done: Contracts in SharePoint and notes in Drive become searchable text, AI fields and SQL rows under Cairn's policies; the counterpart of Openflow's SharePoint and Google Drive connectors
items.note: /v1/document-sources (migration 0122): Microsoft Graph (client credentials) and Drive (service account) listings with subfolders and pages, changed, moved and deleted files followed, Google Docs exported, size limit, keys from secret scopes as the owner. Tested with the real store, catalog and files pipe against a local stand-in for Graph and Drive (tests/test_doc_sources_e2e.py); not yet against a live tenant

items.title: AI gateway for agent code
items.summary: Anthropic- and OpenAI-compatible model endpoints in Cairn, called with Cairn tokens
items.done: Agents written in any framework call models through Cairn: no provider key in agent code, every call as a person or their agent, allowed models, budgets and rate limits, metered and audited; the counterpart of Databricks' Unity Gateway (part 1 of the Agent Bricks counterpart)
items.note: /v1/ai/gateway/anthropic/v1/messages, /v1/ai/gateway/openai/v1/chat/completions, /v1/ai/gateway/models: USE_AI_GATEWAY per model, the agent scope model, shared budgets and allowances, per-person rate limit, streaming passed through and metered. Tested with the official SDKs against a stand-in provider (tests/test_ai_gateway.py)

items.title: Code-first agents: cairn agents init, dev, deploy
items.summary: From an empty directory to a deployed agent app run as the person asking
items.done: A team writes an agent in plain Python, LangGraph or the OpenAI Agents SDK, tests it offline, runs it locally with their own Cairn token, and deploys it without wiring runtime, model keys, sessions or access by hand; the counterpart of Databricks' Agent Bricks CLI
items.note: cairn.agentkit (runtime, ctx with gateway-routed SDK clients and governed SQL, offline test kit, three templates), /v1/agent-apps (migration 0123): an agent identity per app, per-run tokens for the caller narrowed to the app's scopes and revoked after, sessions kept by Cairn, the process runtime and the Kubernetes runtime (a pod per app from the agent runtime image, reached only by Cairn, the chart's Role). Each invocation is an MLflow run in the app's experiment, under the caller's name, metrics only. Tested end to end (tests/test_agent_apps.py, tests/test_agent_apps_mlflow.py against a real MLflow, tests/test_agent_apps_k8s.py on kind)

items.title: Agent trace intelligence
items.summary: What each agent's tool calls and model use say: runs, errors, loops, slow calls, cost, and outliers against its own baseline
items.done: An operator sees which agent is stuck retrying, failing, slowing down or spending far more than it used to, before people complain or the budget runs out; owners see the same for their own agents
items.note: cairn.ai.trace_insights, /v1/agent-traces/insights (and per agent), /v1/agent-traces/settings (admin, audited); every traced tool call records its run (migration 0124): a custom agent's run, an agent app's run token, an OAuth session; key agents' calls are split into sessions. Findings with severity: loops, error rate, refusals, slow calls, flagged text, and volume, cost, latency, calls-per-run and error outliers against the agent's previous weeks. Tested end to end through the real services and HTTP API with real recorded MCP calls from a real agent key, a custom agent's real run and real usage metering (tests/test_agent_trace_insights.py)

items.title: Grounded answers with sources
items.summary: A question answered only from a vector index's passages, citing them
items.done: People ask the support articles or contracts a question and get an answer they can check: every sentence points to the rows it rests on, and Cairn says when the data does not answer it; the counterpart of retrieval-augmented answers in Databricks' and Snowflake's AI layers, under Cairn's policies
items.note: POST /v1/vectors/<name>/answer: passages retrieved as the caller (refused under masks and row filters), numbered and answered by the deployment's model through the metered, budgeted model path; citations actually used [{n, key, chunk, text, score}], sentences without a valid citation flagged, a refusal when no passage supports an answer, audited without content. Tested end to end on a real lakehouse table (tests/test_vectors_answer_e2e.py)

items.title: External Iceberg catalogs, governed
items.summary: Another organisation's or a cloud Iceberg REST catalog queried in Trino as a catalog of its own
items.done: Partner and cloud tables are queried in place under the same grants, masks and row filters as the lakehouse, read-only by default, with their credential never leaving Cairn; the counterpart of Unity Catalog's and Snowflake's catalog federation
items.note: /v1/external-catalogs (migration 0125): registration with a credential reference (secret scope or CAIRN_EXTCAT_*), Trino's dynamic catalogs (CREATE CATALOG by cairn-catalogs only) signing in through Cairn's OAuth token broker with Trino's own key, namespaces, tables and schemas catalogued, read-only enforcement, re-added after a Trino restart. Tested with a second real Cairn Catalog and Store on Trino 484: masked, filtered and refused users, writes refused (tests/test_external_catalogs_e2e.py)

items.title: Share observability
items.summary: Who reads what through each lakehouse share
items.done: Share owners see each recipient's requests, tables read, loads, refusals and failures, find unused and expiring shares and recipients reading tables with failing quality, and are told before a share ends; the counterpart of Delta Sharing's and Snowflake's share usage views
items.note: Per share, day and table counts from Cairn Catalog's per-request questions and the token endpoint, with retention (migration 0125); GET /v1/shares/<name>/usage, GET /v1/shares/usage/overview joined with the quality status; share.expiring and share.unused notices once each. Tested with pyiceberg as the recipient against the real store and catalog (tests/test_share_usage_e2e.py); refusals outside a share's namespaces are decided by the catalog alone and count as requests

items.title: Agents and skills in the marketplace
items.summary: Agent apps, custom agents and extensions listed and requested beside data products
items.done: People find agents and reusable skills where they find data, ask for them with a purpose and duration, and get exactly the right to use them until it expires; the counterpart of Databricks' and Snowflake's marketplace listings of agents and apps
items.note: /marketplace/listings and /marketplace/search (migration 0125): listings by the agent's or skill's owner, searched with data products, requests in the marketplace's queue, approval granting a time-boxed persona with USE_AGENT on urn:li:cairnAgent:<name> (USE_SKILL on urn:li:cairnSkill:<name>) only, revoked by the sweep at expiry and on delisting. Tested through the HTTP API with a real agent app process (tests/test_marketplace_agents.py)

items.title: Agent automations from the CLI: cairn tasks
items.summary: CoWork scheduled tasks and their outbox from a terminal or a script
items.done: Someone who lives in the terminal (or a CI job acting for a person) sets up recurring research, runs it now, reads the report and approves or rejects what goes out, without the web UI
items.note: cairn.agentkit.tasks: list, create (name, prompt, cron, max steps, Slack or email), show (last runs), output (a run's report), run, pause/resume, delete, outbox, approve/reject, --json; CAIRN_URL and CAIRN_TOKEN/CAIRN_TOKEN_FILE from the environment only; agent credentials refused. Tested by running the real CLI in a subprocess against a real Cairn API server, with the report sent to a Slack stand-in only after approval (tests/test_tasks_cli.py)

items.title: Intent-based security for agents
items.summary: Each agent run declares its purpose and the kinds of action it allows; anything else is refused
items.done: An agent asked to summarise revenue cannot, even through a prompt injection or a bug, write, share, export or read tables the task does not concern, though its scopes would allow it; operators can require every agent run to say what it is for
items.note: cairn.identity.intents: intents (purpose, actions read, query, propose, write, share, export, model, admin, tables, domains) on run tokens (agent app invocations), custom agent definitions (migration 0124) and key agents; every agent request classified (HTTP by route, SQL by statement kind, tools by tool) and refused outside its intent (403, audited agent.intent_denied); /v1/agent-intents/settings (require intents, fail closed), /denials, /classify. Tested end to end through the HTTP API with real agent keys, run tokens, a real SQLite warehouse, a custom agent run and a real agent app process whose model call is refused (tests/test_agent_intents.py, tests/test_agent_apps.py)
